text: Balaklava is ahead. After your first sortie I rang that baker in Pechersk and heard him unbolt his door. Now Crimea is waiting for the all-clear. Bondarenko, this is our chance to finish freeing our land.
I remember him digging his feet in at the hangar doors. Today I was still buttoning my jacket when he lowered a wing for me to climb on.
Two hundred and fifty targets over Balaklava. All three aircraft types will be in this wave, with shorter gaps than you’ve seen on any other sortie. I’m staying on the radio until you land.
As we have repeatedly reported, dragons do not exist. As one has just appeared on live television, we’re cutting the broadcast short. Put the weather on. Yesterday’s forecast, preferably.
Quiet at last. Can you hear him breathing? One day I’d like to open my window in Kyiv and just listen to the city waking up.
I can hear him. I’m thinking of that woman from Donetsk with the key in her pocket. I want her to open her own front door again, and I want the two of you back in your hangar. We’ll be waiting.
Understood. Well, my friend? One last sortie. Then home.
